relations.evidence:
Capella supports the following customer key management providers for encryption at rest:

* [AWS Key Management Service](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/)
* [GCP Cloud Key Management](https://cloud.google.com/security/products/security-key-management?hl=en)
* [Azure Key Vault](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/key-vault)

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badges and no literal server-version-string citations anywhere on this 571-line page, despite it being exactly the kind of long reference/prerequisites page where those two known recurring anomalies (docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-edition-badges.json, docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json) tend to show up elsewhere. Neither anomaly recurred in any of this batch's 12 pages - consistent with the batch hypothesis that security/index/project pages are a different authoring lineage than the n1ql/search reference tree where those anomalies were found.

cross_component_finding: The 'Project/Cluster Manager' role name and its '#project-cluster-manager-role' anchor cited here do not literally match cloud/projects/project-roles.md's own table, which names the identical role just 'Cluster Manager'. This is exactly the kind of within-corpus role-naming drift the batch hypothesis asked to watch for, discovered by cross-referencing a management-plane security page against the project-roles page it links to.
cross_product_finding: CMEK's access gate is a genuine 3-role disjunction (Organization Owner OR Project Owner OR Project/Cluster Manager) for project-level Azure CMEK specifically, but a stricter single-role gate (Organization Owner only) for AWS/GCP/org-level-Azure CMEK - the same shape of disjunctive role-gating documented for requiresCapellaRole on the SQL++ statement pages in prior rounds, just with a different, wider role set than the 3-role capella-role:* catalog assembled there (organization-owner/project-owner/project-data-writer). This is direct confirmation of the batch hypothesis: the management-plane UI/API-facing docs reveal more roles and more nuance than the statement pages' distant citations ever showed.
